summary: PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20 extracts Harpaz–Wittenberg, Zéro-cycles sur les espaces homogènes et problème de Galois inverse (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 33 (2020) 775–805, read in the author manuscript). It has 150 items (7 library, 12 planned, 131 missing) and 14 routes. The routes survive the later narrowings of RP.3, IG.0, IG.1, IG.4 and SF.4. The two Part IIs coalesce consistently with the HW16 and HW23 extractions, and their mutual dependency is ordered at stage level. The missing statuses I probed have no other owner. One finding, medium. The paper's two mistakes, E1 on Remarque 4.5 and E2 on the quaternion range, are recorded twice under the same ids: in the extraction and in the reviewed errata file. The records disagree. The errata review narrowed E1 to 'the proof', with rational connectedness only a sufficient repair, and E2 to m ≥ 2. Six hours later the paper review confirmed the extraction's older versions ('a stated result'; m ≥ 3). Both versions now appear in the public register. The extraction's items 75, 104 and 105 follow the superseded versions, and its E1 would need sourceVersions, which it lacks. Fix: reference the errata file, as PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 does, align the three items, and regenerate the register.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Codex codex-a71f92 with a continuation and completion by Claude Code cc-442dc5. Its review is by Claude Code cc-7b31c4, and the errata file is by cc-442dc5, reviewed by codex-hjdg0j. This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did none of them, nor HW16, HW23, or the Part II designs.

All 14 routes and their reasons and briefs, and the status of all 150 items, read in the repository at 6bfc27fb. All 15 cited stage ids exist in the assembled atlas (2840 stages, 8007 edges). Five have since been narrowed, and the routed items still fall within what they keep. RS-03 narrows RP.3 to 'geometric torsors, twists, descent and étale-Brauer–Manin comparisons', which fits route 7's torus-descent items. RS-29 narrows IG.0, IG.1 and IG.4, which still cover π₁ of G/H and local constraints on embedding problems (routes 9 and 11). RS-25 narrows SF.4, which keeps 'source-scoped alterations, modifications and proved resolution settings' (route 4).

The two Part IIs: route 13 (HomogeneousMassey) and route 14 (ZeroCycles) coalesce with PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23 R8 and PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-16 R11 under identical ids and titles. Every result shared across the three papers goes to the same Part II in each: HW16 Conjecture 9.1, Corollaries 8.4(1) and 9.25, Theorem 8.3(3) and Lemma 8.2. The two Part IIs depend on each other at item level. ZeroCycles' Theorem A uses HomogeneousMassey's universal torsors and finite-stabilizer results (§§3, 5), and HomogeneousMassey's Theorem 6.6 and Remark 4.5 use ZeroCycles' rational-connectedness items. Both briefs say so and prescribe a stage order without a cycle ('The generic RC geometry exported by HeightsRationalPointsPartIIZeroCycles precedes this homogeneous layer'). PROTOCOL requires acyclicity only at stage level, so this is not a finding.

Ownership of rational connectedness: no stage in the atlas mentions rational connectedness, Graber–Harris–Starr or rationally chain connected varieties. SF.4, 'Deformations, models and birational geometry', was narrowed by RS-25 to exclude it. So the ZeroCycles Part II is the only planned owner. PAPER-BENOIST-WITTENBERG-20 uses the notion at MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.7 without defining it; that is a matter for that extraction.

Missing statuses probed against possible owners: H³(k, G_m) = 0 (item 35). Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 10's H³ is H³(Gal(L/K), L^×) at finite level, not Tate's vanishing. Also probed: Pic(G) = 0 and the units of simply connected groups (items 80 and 140; neither Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups nor ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0a–RG2.4 plans them); unipotent homogeneous spaces (items 146–147; Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 5 plans unipotent groups but not their Galois cohomology); and the Hasse principle and local H¹ vanishing for simply connected groups (item 93; AA.4 plans weak approximation 'only in the cases justified by the relevant group theorem'). The missing statuses stand.

Duplication across extractions: searched every papers/*.result.json for zero-cycles, Massey, homogeneous spaces, Borovoi, Grunwald, the fibration method, universal torsors and descent. Apart from HW16 and HW23 (coalesced, as above), the hits are unrelated uses of the same words (special zero-cycles, symmetric spaces, Grunwald–Wang in automorphy lifting routed to R02.2/R02.4). IG.4 already takes Khare–Wintenberger's Grunwald–Wang item, consistently with route 11.

Source issues: compared the extraction's E1–E2 with the errata file and its review, REV-ERRATA-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20, and read both entries in REGISTER.md and data/source-issues.json (finding 1). Tried the published JAMS PDF on 2026-09-30. Both ams.org paths returned a Cloudflare challenge and pubs.ams.org a login viewer, so, like the extraction and both reviews, I could not compare the version of record.
Library: the seven library items were verified by the review at the pins. I did not re-open them.

findings.claim: The paper's two mistakes are recorded twice under the same ids, and the two records disagree. The extraction's own sourceIssues and the errata file both carry E1 and E2. The errata review (REV-ERRATA-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20, 23 September 12:34 UTC) narrowed both. For E1 (Remarque 4.5 applies Theorem 4.2(i) without its rational-connectedness hypothesis), it changed 'affects' from 'a stated result' to 'the proof'. Adding rational connectedness of X is only a sufficient restricted repair, not a demonstrated necessary hypothesis, because Proposition 3.3(i) gives a geometric section without it. For E2 (the quaternion range 'm ≥ 1'), it changed the correction from m ≥ 3 to m ≥ 2 in Demarche's convention, where Q₄ ≅ C₄. Six hours later the paper review confirmed the extraction's un-narrowed versions without reconciling them. So both versions are now in the public register under the same ids, with different 'affects' values and incompatible corrections. The extraction's items follow the superseded versions. Item 75's note presents rational connectedness as the correction, and items 104 and 105 restrict to 'the standard generalized-quaternion range m≥3'. The extraction's E1 also claims 'a stated result' without the sourceVersions list that §18 then requires. The check passes only because check_paper.py does not enforce that rule.
findings.evidence: Extraction E1: kind gap, affects 'a stated result', correction 'Add the hypothesis that X is rationally connected …'. Extraction E2: correction 'm ≥ 3 (for m = 2 the presentation gives the cyclic group of order 4 …)'. errata/PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.json E1: affects 'the proof', review (by REV-ERRATA-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20): 'Changed affects from a stated result to the proof: no counterexample to the implication was found …'. The correction says 'Adding rational connectedness of X is a sufficient restricted repair, not a demonstrated necessary hypothesis … Proposition3.3(i) already provides a geometric section without rational connectedness.' Errata E2 correction: 'Use m ≥ 2 if following the convention in the cited Demarche author manuscript, which includes Q_4≅C_4 …'. Its review: 'with the correction amended from m≥3 to m≥2 in the cited source's convention'. Git: errata review e3c377e9, 2026-09-23 12:34 UTC (#2257); paper review 5069b0bd, 2026-09-23 18:28 UTC (#2444), whose report says 'both sourceIssues confirmed' and restates E1 as '(gap, a stated result)' and E2 as m ≥ 3. data/source-issues.json lists four HW20 entries: E1 twice (affects 'a stated result' from the result file, 'the proof' from the errata file) and E2 twice. research/errata/REGISTER.md lines 8054–8057 print all four under 'PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20'. Item 104: 'For a constant generalized quaternion group Q_(2^m), m≥3 … use the standard generalized-quaternion range m≥3'; item 105: '… generalized quaternion Γ=Q_(2^m), m≥3'. The extraction has no sourceVersions, and its source.version says the publisher PDF 'returned 403 and was not read'. scripts/check_errata.py:35–38 requires sourceVersions when an issue affects a stated result. Precedent for a single record: PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18.result.json carries sourceIssueReferences pointing to its errata file 'to avoid duplicate entries'.
findings.fix: Keep one record per mistake: the reviewed errata file. In the extraction, replace sourceIssues E1–E2 by sourceIssueReferences: [{'file': 'research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.json', 'ids': ['PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/E1', 'PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/E2'], 'note': 'Recorded and reviewed there (REV-ERRATA-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20); E1 affects the proof, E2 uses m ≥ 2 with Q_4 = C_4'}], as PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 does. Rewrite item 75's note: rational connectedness of X is a sufficient restricted repair, and the remark's full generality needs the section-based fibration variant, via Proposition 3.3(i), stated and justified. Keep G1 open. In items 104 and 105, state m ≥ 2 with Q_4 = C_4, or m ≥ 3 explicitly for non-abelian groups, and cite E2 rather than calling m ≥ 3 'the standard range'. Correct REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.md's account of E1 and E2. Re-run check_paper.py and scripts/errata.py so that REGISTER.md and data/source-issues.json list each mistake once.
